property_summary: Calling settle() reverts whenever the caller has not previously locked in a guess (no prior lockInGuess call, or already settled).
After a caller locks in a guess in the current transaction, settle() reverts because the target block has not yet been reached.
lockInGuess reverts if and only if the sent value is not exactly 1 ether (for a fresh guesser).
Even after locking in a guess, settle() reverts while the current block has not passed the target block, and it must be callable with no Ether attached in that case.
Once a guess is locked in, any subsequent lockInGuess call by the same address reverts, regardless of the value sent or the guess.
After lockInGuess, a settle() call in the same or immediately following transaction (before the target block passes) reverts and leaves the contract's balance unchanged.
After a successful lockInGuess, a second lockInGuess call reverts and leaves the contract's Ether balance unchanged.
Calling settle() on C when no guess has been locked in (fresh contract) always reverts and leaves the contract's Ether balance unchanged.
A lockInGuess call with msg.value != 1 ether reverts and does not consume the caller's one-shot guess slot, so a subsequent correctly-funded lockInGuess succeeds and deposits exactly 1 ether.
A correctly funded lockInGuess with any guess always succeeds, transfers exactly 1 ether into C, and deducts exactly 1 ether from the caller.
After lockInGuess, settle() always reverts until the locked block number has passed, and it does not unlock the guess (a subsequent lockInGuess still reverts).
Calling settle() when no guess is locked always reverts and leaves C's ether balance unchanged.
